questions.hint: Read the three digits of \(809\) from left to right: the first digit is hundreds, the middle digit is tens, and the last digit is ones.

keyPoints.text: how is \(809\) written on the numeral expander
keyPoints.note: In a 3-digit number, the first digit on the left shows hundreds, the middle digit shows tens, and the last digit on the right shows ones.

questions.solution: \(809\) has \(8\) hundreds, \(0\) tens, and \(9\) ones.

steps.explain: Look at the first digit on the left of \(809\): the hundreds digit is \(8\) (highlighted in yellow).

questions.stem: Round each number to the nearest \(10\). Numbers that end with a \(5\) are rounded up. In j, what is \(99\) rounded to the nearest \(10\)?

keyPoints.note: Check the ones digit: 4 or less rounds down to the lower multiple of 10, while 5 or more rounds up to the next multiple of 10.

questions.solution: \(99\) lies between \(90\) and \(100\). Since its ones digit is \(9\), \(99\) rounds to \(100\).

meta.question: 6j

questions.stem: Write some numbers and round them to the nearest \(10\). Which list shows all three numbers correctly rounded to the nearest \(10\)?
questions.hint: Check the ones digit of each number: \(5\) or more rounds up to the next \(10\), and \(4\) or less rounds down.

keyPoints.note: Check each number's ones digit: 5 or more rounds up to the next ten, and 4 or less rounds down to the lower ten.

questions.solution: \(45\) rounds up to \(50\), \(74\) rounds down to \(70\), and \(168\) rounds up to \(170\).

steps.explain: Check the first number \(45\): numbers ending in \(5\) round up to the next \(10\), so \(45 \rightarrow 50\).
Check the second number \(74\): its ones digit is \(4\) (less than \(5\)), so it rounds down to \(70\).
Check the third number \(168\): its ones digit is \(8\) (\(5\) or more), so it rounds up to \(170\).
Combine all three rounded results: \(45 \rightarrow 50,\; 74 \rightarrow 70,\; 168 \rightarrow 170\).
